panels.title: Ordering p50
panels.description: Cumulative median across validators.

panels.title: Materialized p50
panels.description: Cumulative median across validators.
Committee commit throughput. Each worker observes the same stream, so the query uses max, not sum.
panels.title: Committed bytes/s
Views sealed/s
panels.description: Median per-validator seal rate. Do not sum replicated view seals.

panels.title: Seal route mix (stacked views/s, median validator)
panels.description: Stacked median route rates. The unstacked total is their sum.

panels.title: Fallback seal routes/s (median validator)
panels.description: Median rate of non-fast seal routes. Sustained nonzero values indicate degraded consensus.
Median worker observation of the replicated commit stream.
panels.title: Committed TPS (median validator)

panels.description: Run-cumulative submission-to-ordering latency. Values are medians of per-worker percentiles.
panels.title: Ordering latency (median across workers, p50/p95)

panels.description: Run-cumulative latency through local payload materialization. Values are medians of per-worker percentiles.
panels.title: Materialized latency (median across workers, p50/p95)
Core thread busy (median validator)
panels.description: Median VantageCore wall-time utilization. It includes measured waits; 100% means the core task is saturated.

panels.title: Core wall time by operation (stacked, median validator)
panels.description: Median wall-time utilization by core operation. The total sums the displayed medians.
Difference between the highest and lowest sequence heads. It must return to zero after catch-up.
panels.title: Sequence spread

targets.expr: max((sum by (node) (rate(utilization_timer{node=~"$node",node=~".*-primary$",proc=~"inbound_dispatch|effect_execution|payload_sync|timer_firing|header_seal|resume_tick|metrics_tick|avail_flush"}[1m])) and on(node) protocol_info{protocol="vantage"})) / 10000 or vector(0)

panels.description: Busiest VantageCore thread. Sustained 100% means saturation.
panels.title: Worst core busy

targets.expr: max(100 * max by (queue) (worker_queue_peak{node=~"$node",node=~".*-worker-0$"}) / max by (queue) (worker_queue_capacity{node=~"$node",node=~".*-worker-0$"})) or vector(0)

panels.description: Highest one-second queue utilization across worker stages and validators.
panels.title: Worst worker queue

panels.description: Protocol fault counters and process panics. Must stay zero.
panels.title: Critical faults

panels.description: Per-second view rates. Resolver seals identify target-local fallback decisions.
panels.title: View entry / seal / direct resolver rates
View lag and active resolver targets
panels.description: Clamped data-view gaps and target-local resolver instances awaiting a terminal decision.

panels.title: View frontiers (pacemaker / responsive / output)
panels.description: Pacemaker, proposal, and output frontiers should remain within a few views.

panels.title: Pacemaker wish / entry (views)
panels.description: Healthy order: omega_q >= entry target >= entered view, with own watermark ahead.

panels.title: Availability confirmations/s by node
panels.description: Logical confirmations remain active in every mode. Wire traffic uses per-block ACKs, periodic watermarks, or default echo claims.

panels.title: Repairs requested / served per node (Vantage / Simple-IT)

panels.description: Submitted traffic is additive. Committed traffic is replicated, so the query uses max across worker-0 observations.
panels.title: Submitted / committed transactions/s
Published block size (run-to-date)
panels.description: Run-cumulative block-size percentiles and maximum. The maximum never decreases.
Primary plus worker CPU per validator, excluding the client. Values may exceed one logical core.
panels.title: CPU usage (per validator, % of one core)

panels.description: Primary plus worker resident memory per validator, excluding the client.
panels.title: Memory usage (RSS, per validator)
VantageCore utilization by section (% wall-clock busy)
panels.description: Wall-time utilization by core section. Await time is included; 100% means the single core task is saturated.

targets.expr: (100 * (sum by (node) (rate(utilization_timer{node=~"$node",node=~".*-primary$",proc=~"inbound_dispatch|effect_execution|payload_sync|timer_firing|header_seal|resume_tick|metrics_tick|avail_flush"}[1m])) - sum by (node) (rate(core_wait_timer{node=~"$node",node=~".*-primary$"}[1m]))) / 1e6) and on(node) protocol_info{protocol="vantage"}

panels.title: Vantage core CPU / wait
panels.description: Estimated compute time is utilization minus measured store waits. Unmeasured network waits make compute an upper bound.

panels.title: VantageCore inbound-queue depth (now / peak)
panels.description: Current and one-second peak inbound depth. Rising peak means burst backlog; rising current depth means sustained backlog.

panels.title: Primary TCP sessions / peers
panels.description: Open inbound sessions and distinct validator IPs. Extra sessions come from separate sender pools.

panels.title: Worker TCP sessions / peers
panels.description: Open inbound sessions and distinct validator IPs. Payload repair can open additional sessions.

panels.title: Messages/s sent by category (stacked)
panels.description: Every wire type has one category. A positive uncategorized value indicates a missing mapping.

panels.title: Bytes/s sent by category (stacked)
panels.description: Every wire type has one category. A positive uncategorized value indicates a missing mapping.
Per-validator wire bytes divided by sequenced bytes. Overhead equals the displayed value minus one.
panels.title: Wire bytes sent per sequenced byte (per validator)

panels.description: Per-validator. Higher is worse (it is amplification, not efficiency).
panels.title: Wire bytes sent per 512B-normalized tx (per validator)
Wire sent (committee total)
panels.description: Committee-wide wire send rate.

panels.title: Wire received (committee total)
panels.description: Committee-wide wire receive rate, including client ingress.

panels.title: Worker queue utilization
panels.description: Worst-validator one-second peak by stage. Sustained 100% identifies a blocked stage.

panels.title: Store loop health
panels.description: Peak loop age should stay below 50 ms. Panics must stay zero.

panels.title: Sequence recording lag
panels.description: Must stay zero. Persistent lag means terminal views were not recorded.

panels.title: Checkpoint agreement
panels.description: Distinct heads must be one. Validators compared shows the sample size.

panels.title: Sequence recording
panels.description: Record and cursor rates should match. Rejections must stay zero.

panels.title: Checkpoint announcements
panels.description: A checkpoint certifies at f+1 counted announcements. Repeats may be ignored; equivocators must stay zero.

panels.title: State transfer
panels.description: Started transfers should become verified. Exhaustion and queue drops must stay zero.

panels.title: Sequence verification
panels.description: Verified lead should return to zero after catch-up. Mismatches must stay zero.

panels.title: Sequence installation
panels.description: Pending views and blocks should drain while headers arrive and views apply. Failed and rejected must stay zero.

panels.title: Primary network RTT by validator
panels.description: Mean kernel TCP RTT sampled when each distinct peer first connects.

panels.title: Worker network RTT by validator
panels.description: Mean kernel TCP RTT sampled when each distinct peer first connects.
